importanceModel.source: Official enhanced ACT reporting-category ranges + mapped ACT practice-bank frequency
importanceModel.domainWeightNormalization: official reporting-category midpoint / highest midpoint in the same ACT section
importanceModel.topicFrequencyNormalization: mapped topic question count / highest mapped topic question count in the same reporting category

questionInventory.selectionRule: Two mapped questions per ACT lesson are used as Study Guide exit-ticket checks and removed from the standalone Topic Quiz.

metadata.note: ACT package template generated from the complete Web exam-prep materials.

topics.title: Identify the essay's overall purpose
topics.description: Recognize the essay's main claim and supporting evidence. Use a Purpose-Frame Scan to prefer revisions that strengthen that central claim and reject those that alter the purpose.

topics.title: Identify the function of a paragraph or sentence
topics.description: Recognize whether a sentence states main idea, provides example, shows consequence, or shifts topic. Use topic words and signal markers to assign one concise function label.

topics.title: Judge whether a sentence's information is relevant to the central purpose
topics.description: Identify whether the sentence provides evidence, explanation, or a necessary transition for the paragraph's purpose. Use a one-phrase purpose and a yes/no check to keep or delete it.

topics.title: Add the detail that best supports the central idea
topics.description: Recognize the paragraph’s main idea and compare sentences for topical fit. Eliminate new-topic or repetitive choices and pick a concrete example or effect.

topics.title: Delete off-topic, repetitive, or irrelevant information
topics.description: You will recognize sentences that add no new support or repeat earlier wording. Delete units that neither clarify the topic sentence nor provide essential transitions or necessary detail.

topics.title: Choose the revision that best accomplishes a specified writing goal
topics.description: Recognize revisions that align wording and tone with the specified writing goal. Restate the goal and eliminate choices that add topics, weaken claims, or stray from focus.

topics.title: Place a sentence in the most logical position within a paragraph
topics.description: Recognize the sentence’s main idea and exact referents (who, what, when). Anchor it by matching referents and pronoun/topic flow so it clarifies, continues, or concludes.

topics.title: Arrange the logical order of paragraphs
topics.description: Identify each paragraph’s main idea and connective cue (cause, contrast, example, conclusion). Insert the paragraph where its opening connects back and its content prefaces the next.

topics.title: Choose the best insertion point for a sentence
topics.description: Recognize which nearby sentence repeats a new sentence’s core referent. Underline the referent and insert where that idea continues the paragraph.

topics.title: Determine the best place to insert a paragraph
topics.description: Recognize the anchor sentence and compare surrounding sentence focus. Choose the spot where the paragraph adds explanation using continuation words and consistent topic focus.

topics.title: Choose an intra- or inter-paragraph transition
topics.description: Identify the two units a transition must connect and their relationship. Choose the option with a signal word that indicates addition, contrast, cause, or time and keeps subjects and tense.

topics.title: Maintain clear pronoun referents and information flow
topics.description: Recognize ambiguous pronouns and their nearest noun antecedents. Replace or name antecedents and reorder phrases so the referent immediately precedes the pronoun.

topics.title: Choose an effective introductory sentence
topics.description: Identify the paragraph’s main topic and scope from sentence-level cues. Prefer intros that narrow from general to specific and avoid new topics or repeated details.

topics.title: Choose an effective conclusion
topics.description: Recognize how the last sentence echoes the paragraph’s main idea and tone. Restate the core idea in fresh words and end with a logical writing move.

topics.title: Maintain paragraph unity and overall focus
topics.description: Recognize sentences that do not support the paragraph’s single main idea. Name the main idea, then remove or rewrite sentences lacking a clear link.

topics.title: Choose the most precise word or phrase for context
topics.description: Recognize whether a word's intensity matches surrounding modifiers and verbs. Use intensity signals and tone to eliminate under- or overstated choices.

topics.title: Eliminate redundant words or information
topics.description: Recognize overlapping word pairs that repeat meaning. Underline the core word and pick the shortest phrasing that preserves necessary detail.

topics.title: Avoid vague pronouns and ambiguity
topics.description: You will recognize ambiguous pronouns by comparing nearby antecedents and matching number, gender, and meaning. Circle the pronoun, underline two possible antecedents, and replace the pronoun with a specific noun.

topics.title: Replace wordy phrasing with a more concise, direct expression
topics.description: Recognize wordy signal phrases and concise alternatives in sentences. Swap the flagged wording for one grammatically fitting expression and adjust surrounding grammar to preserve meaning.

topics.title: Choose the idiomatic English collocation or expression
topics.description: Recognize the most natural verb-noun or verb-preposition collocation in a sentence. Prefer common grammar chunks; say the short native sentence and choose the option with strongest collocation evidence.

topics.title: Maintain a consistent level of formality
topics.description: Compare the marked sentence's tone to the paragraph's dominant register. Swap words or contractions and adjust sentence length; read aloud to confirm consistent formality.

topics.title: Maintain consistent author tone and voice
topics.description: You will recognize tone using nearby vocabulary and sentence rhythm. Rewrite to match two tone adjectives, compare key words, then adjust one element.

topics.title: Make expression appropriate for the audience and purpose
topics.description: Recognize when wording clashes with the intended audience and purpose. Replace casual words, slang, and contractions with neutral, precise alternatives to set an appropriate tone.

topics.title: Avoiding abrupt, colloquial, or out-of-register wording
topics.description: Recognize phrases that sound colloquial or abrupt within a formal paragraph. Label each phrase's discourse role and replace it with a concise, formal alternative, then read aloud for smooth flow.

topics.title: Improve sentence rhythm and expressive effectiveness
topics.description: You will recognize excess modifiers and uneven clause rhythms. Trim one nonessential phrase and restructure remaining elements into parallel units.

topics.title: Identify independent clauses and subordinate (dependent) clauses
topics.description: Recognize whether a highlighted clause has its own subject, main verb, and a complete thought. Tag clauses INDEPENDENT or SUBORDINATE and select punctuation that preserves the main clause.

topics.title: Fixing Sentence Fragments
topics.description: Recognize incomplete clauses, -ing phrases, and missing subjects or finite verbs. Attach, add a subject and finite verb, or recast as a modifier without creating comma splices.

topics.title: Correcting Run-on Sentences
topics.description: Spot two independent clauses joined without proper punctuation. Split into sentences, insert a semicolon, or add a comma and coordinating conjunction.

topics.title: Fix a comma splice
topics.description: Recognize when two independent clauses are joined only by a comma. Then replace-or-connect using a semicolon, comma+coordinating conjunction, period, or subordinate restructuring based on meaning.

topics.title: Correctly join independent and dependent clauses
topics.description: Recognize independent versus dependent clauses by locating the subject, finite verb, and any subordinating word. Then pick subordinators, comma+coordinators, or semicolons to match the relationship and punctuation.

topics.title: Fix dangling or misplaced modifiers
topics.description: Identify modifiers missing a clear actor and the noun they should modify. Underline that noun and rewrite so the actor immediately follows the modifier with an active verb.

topics.title: Maintain parallel structure
topics.description: Recognize mismatched grammatical forms among list items and clauses. Match each item’s part of speech and revise to the same form, then check connectors and punctuation.

topics.title: Establish a clear, logical comparison structure
topics.description: Recognize the two items compared and the comparison marker. Rewrite to repeat nouns and make qualities parallel and unambiguous.

topics.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
topics.description: Recognize which noun is the true subject despite intervening phrases or clauses. Apply the proximity rule: make the verb agree with the subject closest to it.

topics.title: Pronoun–Antecedent Agreement
topics.description: Identify the nearest antecedent noun and whether it is singular or plural. Match pronoun number and gender or revise to "his or her" or a plural noun for clarity.

topics.title: Pronoun case and pronoun reference
topics.description: You will recognize a pronoun's grammatical role and its antecedent in a sentence. Label subject/object/prepositional roles and substitute the single pronoun to pick subjective, objective, or reflexive case.

topics.title: Verb tense, voice, and sequence of tenses
topics.description: Recognize the base timeline by comparing verb forms as evidence. Match reporting verbs to that timeline and use would/was going to for future-in-past.

topics.title: Verb forms and non-finite verb structures (infinitives, gerunds, participles)
topics.description: Recognize whether a phrase functions as a main verb, auxiliary verb phrase, gerund, infinitive, or participial modifier. Replace mentally with the simplest correct form and check attachment, agreement, and parallelism.

topics.title: Adjective vs. adverb usage
topics.description: Recognize whether a modifier describes a noun or an action by locating its target word. Then substitute 'how' versus 'which/what kind' to choose the adverb (-ly) or adjective form.

topics.title: Singular vs. plural noun forms and noun-number agreement
topics.description: You will recognize noun-and-quantifier pairs and incorrect plural forms in phrases. Use quantifier cues to choose singular, irregular plural, or uncountable noun forms.

topics.title: Confusable words and standard word meanings
topics.description: Recognize when a confusable word clashes with sentence grammar or intended meaning. Name the intended meaning, swap the standard word matching grammar, and read the sentence aloud to confirm.

topics.title: Comma after introductory element
topics.description: Recognize introductory chunks—dependent clauses, participial phrases, or long prepositional phrases. Place one comma after them; omit it for very short openings or when they act as the subject.

topics.title: Use commas to set off nonrestrictive (nonessential) clauses or phrases
topics.description: Recognize clauses that do not identify the noun and function as extra information. Place commas immediately before and after the clause and test by reading the sentence without it.

topics.title: Commas in lists and coordinate modifiers
topics.description: Recognize when three or more parallel items or modifiers independently modify a noun. Place commas after each item and include a comma before the final and for rhythm and clarity.

topics.title: Joining independent clauses with a coordinating conjunction
topics.description: Recognize when both sides of a conjunction contain complete clauses with subjects and verbs. If both are independent clauses, place a comma immediately before the coordinating conjunction; otherwise omit it.

topics.title: Use a semicolon to join two independent clauses
topics.description: Recognize when each side has a subject and verb and stands alone. If both are independent and related, join with a semicolon; if not, subordinate or rewrite.

topics.title: Use a colon to introduce an explanation or a list
topics.description: Recognize whether the words before the blank form an independent clause. Insert a colon when what follows directly explains or lists items without an extra conjunction or comma.

topics.title: Using dashes to mark insertions, emphasis, or abrupt shifts
topics.description: You will recognize interrupting phrases set off by dashes and the absence of surrounding commas. Place matching dashes around the interruption and omit commas to create an emphatic, abrupt break.

topics.title: Using parentheses for supplemental (nonessential) information
topics.description: Recognize nonessential asides by removing them to see if the sentence stays grammatically complete. Use the Parenthetical Purpose Check to pick commas, parentheses, or dashes by tone and integration.

topics.title: Apostrophes show possession or omission
topics.description: Recognize the noun owner and its singular or plural form. If singular, add 's; if plural ending in s, add only an apostrophe.

topics.title: Sentence-ending punctuation with direct quotations
topics.description: Recognize whether quoted words are a question, exclamation, or neither based on their wording. Decide punctuation placement using the quote internal rule and avoid doubling terminal marks.

topics.title: Rational-number operations, ordering, and absolute value
topics.description: Recognize each expression's distance-from-zero and the resulting nonnegative value. Sign out absolute values, apply leading negatives, then convert to a common form to compare numerically.

topics.title: Convert between fractions, decimals, and percentages
topics.description: You will visualize decimal-point shifts and compare magnitudes across representations. Shift the decimal two places, attach a percent sign, and confirm magnitude against the original number.

topics.title: Real-number properties and number-line relationships
topics.description: Visualize points and the midpoint on the number line from endpoint coordinates. Average x1 and x2 for the midpoint, then add/subtract the distance to move right or left.

topics.title: Performing arithmetic operations with complex numbers
topics.description: Recognize and separate real and imaginary parts after expanding binomials with i. FOIL, replace i squared with -1, then combine like-variable terms.

topics.title: Powers of i and complex conjugates
topics.description: Recognize the real and imaginary parts after using a conjugate. Reduce i^n by n mod 4 and combine like parts.

topics.title: Laws for Integer Exponents
topics.description: Recognize common numeric factors and repeated variables in a fractional expression. Factor to cancel bases, subtract denominator exponents from numerator exponents, then compute remaining powers.

topics.title: Negative and fractional exponents
topics.description: Recognize common bases, fractional exponents, and negatives in expressions. Rewrite with one base, combine exponents using (a^m)^n and a^p·a^q, then convert negatives to reciprocals.

topics.title: Simplify and operate with square-root expressions
topics.description: Recognize perfect-square factors and like radicals inside radicands. Factor to extract integer squares, simplify remaining roots, then combine like radicals by adding coefficients.

topics.title: Convert between exponent and radical forms (fractional exponents)
topics.description: Recognize when expressions like ⁿ√(x^m) and x^{m/n} represent the same power of x. Rewrite radicals as fractional exponents and subtract like exponents, then reduce fractions.

topics.title: Rationalizing the denominator
topics.description: You will recognize a radical in the denominator and the conjugate form. Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate, use difference of squares, then simplify common factors.

topics.title: Direct and inverse proportional relationships
topics.description: Recognize how y scales with one direct and one inverse variable. Form y = k·(direct)/(inverse), find k from given numbers, then substitute to compute y.

topics.title: Unit rates: speed and density
topics.description: Recognize rates as distance per time versus mass per volume and match units. Compute each unit rate (distance÷time, mass÷volume), keep units, then divide to simplify.

topics.title: Percent and Percent Change
topics.description: Recognize successive percent increases and decreases and their effects on price or quantity. Convert each percent to a multiplier and multiply factors to compute the net percent change.

topics.title: Unit conversion and dimensional analysis
topics.description: Recognize chained units and how they multiply or cancel in volume problems. Convert measures to meters, form m^3, then apply 1 m^3 = 1000 L.

topics.title: Scale interpretation and order-of-magnitude estimation
topics.description: Recognize how a model measurement maps to real distance via the scale. Convert scale to units per model unit, multiply, and round to one significant digit.

topics.title: Vector components, magnitude, and direction
topics.description: Visualize how components ⟨x,y⟩ determine a vector's length and quadrant. Compute √(x^2+y^2), find α = arctan(|y/x|), and map α to θ by quadrant.

topics.title: Vector addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication
topics.description: Visualize how each scalar stretches components and how subtraction becomes adding a negated vector. Multiply components, replace subtraction with the scaled negative, and add corresponding components while tracking signs.

topics.title: Matrix addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication
topics.description: Recognize how scalar factors change each matrix entry and compare corresponding entries across matrices. Multiply every entry by its scalar and subtract corresponding entries to form the result matrix.

topics.title: Matrix multiplication as representation of composing linear transformations
topics.description: Visualize how matrix products represent composing linear transformations and the order of application. Place the first-applied matrix on the right, multiply row-by-column, and simplify entries.

topics.title: 2×2 determinants and basic 2×2 matrix equations
topics.description: Recognize when determinant ad−bc and entries make a 2×2 system invertible. Swap diagonals, negate off-diagonals, divide by ad−bc, and multiply by the constant vector to get x.

topics.title: Solve a single-variable linear equation
topics.description: Recognize variable terms, coefficients, constants, and parentheses in a linear equation. Distribute, collect like terms, then isolate the variable with inverse operations.

topics.title: Single-variable linear inequality
topics.description: Recognize how variable and constant terms move during inequality simplification. Combine like terms, isolate the variable, and reverse the sign if dividing by negative.

topics.title: Absolute-value equations and inequalities
topics.description: Recognize how isolating |ax+b| yields two linear cases to compare. Isolate the absolute expression, split into ± cases, then combine solutions by intersection or union.

topics.title: Slope, intercepts, and equation of a line
topics.description: You will recognize intercepts as points and visualize slope between variables. Use (a,0) and (0,b) to compute m and plug into y=mx+b.

topics.title: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
topics.description: You will recognize which variable's coefficients can be matched and eliminated. Multiply to match coefficients, add or subtract to remove that variable, then substitute to find the other.

topics.title: Interpreting parameters and solutions of a linear model in context
topics.description: Recognize fixed parameters and per-unit rates in a contextual linear equation. Label variables with units, solve for the unknown, and state the numeric result in context.

topics.title: Factor quadratic expressions
topics.description: Recognize two integers whose product equals a·c and whose sum equals b. Split bx into those terms, factor each group, and extract the common binomial.

topics.title: Solve quadratic equations by completing the square
topics.description: Recognize when ax^2+bx is present so a perfect square can form. Move constants, divide by a if needed, add (b/2a)^2, then take ± square roots.

topics.title: Discriminant and number of real roots
topics.description: Recognize how the discriminant predicts the number of real roots. Compute D = b^2 − 4ac exactly and apply the sign test, checking subtractions to avoid errors.

topics.title: Zeros, Vertex, and Axis of Symmetry of a Quadratic
topics.description: Identify a quadratic's zeros, vertex, and axis from its coefficients. Compute x = -b/(2a), plug in to get y, factor or use root formula, and check axis as zeros' midpoint.

topics.title: Systems of quadratic equations and quadratic inequalities
topics.description: Recognize when two quadratic expressions produce a single quadratic in x. Set the expressions equal, rewrite ax^2+bx+c=0, and use b^2-4ac to count real x.

topics.title: Polynomial operations: factoring polynomials
topics.description: Recognize a greatest common factor in coefficients and x-powers across all terms. Extract the GCF, factor the leftover quadratic by product-sum, and multiply back the GCF.

topics.title: Remainder Theorem and Factor Theorem
topics.description: Recognize x − a gives substitution a and f(a) equals the remainder. Substitute a into f; if f(a)=0, x − a is a factor.

topics.title: Polynomial zeros, multiplicity, and end behavior
topics.description: Recognize each zero and its multiplicity from the polynomial's factors and leading coefficient. Use multiplicity to decide crossing versus touching and degree plus leading coefficient to predict end behavior.

topics.title: Simplify a rational expression and state domain restrictions
topics.description: Recognize matching factors and the x-values that make the denominator zero. Factor completely, cancel nonzero common factors, and list every excluded x-value as the domain restriction.

topics.title: Check for extraneous solutions in rational equations (verify domain restrictions)
topics.description: You will recognize values of the variable that make any denominator zero. List domain exclusions, solve algebraically, then substitute candidates to reject extraneous solutions.

topics.title: Solve a radical equation and check for extraneous roots
topics.description: Recognize algebraic roots and check whether they satisfy the original radical expression and domain constraints. Isolate the radical, square, then test each root and discard extraneous solutions.

topics.title: Solve exponential equations by expressing both sides with the same base
topics.description: Identify when both sides can use the same base to compare exponents and variables. Rewrite as common-base powers and set exponents equal to solve.

topics.title: Exponential Growth and Decay
topics.description: Recognize how repeated percent changes alter quantities using multipliers. Convert r to 1±r, raise to t, then multiply by the initial amount.

topics.title: Logarithm definition and basic properties
topics.description: Recognize splitting a log argument into numeric factors and variable powers. Factor, use sum and power rules, then substitute the known log value.

topics.title: Solving logarithmic equations with domain checks
topics.description: Recognize valid variable values by checking each logarithm's argument is positive. Record domain constraints, combine like-base logs, convert to exponential form, and verify solutions satisfy those constraints.

topics.title: Define a variable from a real-world context
topics.description: You will recognize the single concrete quantity to count or measure and its unit. Assign a short symbol with its unit in words and check domain constraints (nonnegative, integer).

topics.title: Translate a verbal condition into an inequality or equation
topics.description: Recognize signal words and boundary inclusivity in verbal conditions. Use the Signal-Boundary-Relation rule to compute numeric bounds and choose the correct inequality symbol for the variable.

topics.title: Form a system of equations from given constraints
topics.description: Recognize independent constraints and corresponding variable units in word problems. Define two variables with units, write one equation per constraint, then choose substitution or elimination.

topics.title: Interpret a solution's units, range, and feasibility
topics.description: Recognize which candidate x values match the problem's units and domain. Attach units, apply explicit limits, and use comparative language to reject infeasible values.

topics.title: Determine whether a relation is a function
topics.description: Recognize each domain element and its paired outputs. Scan distinct inputs; if any input has multiple different outputs, it's not a function.

topics.title: Function notation and evaluating function values
topics.description: Recognize how the input replaces every x and how negatives need parentheses. Substitute the value, follow order of operations, and track signs carefully.

topics.title: Domain and Range
topics.description: Recognize how interior expressions (radicands, denominators) restrict x-values and how those x-constraints map to outputs. Isolate interior restrictions, evaluate extreme allowed inputs, and test monotonic behavior to form the range.

topics.title: Translate between a function's table, graph, formula, and real-world context
topics.description: Compare a table, graph, and formula using input–output pairs. Use two distinct (x,y) pairs to compute slope and find b in y=mx+b.

topics.title: Evaluating and interpreting piecewise functions
topics.description: Recognize which branch's domain contains the input x and compare boundary inequalities. Use inequality checks, substitute x into that branch's formula, and verify the result.

topics.title: Linear and quadratic functions: solving for intersection points
topics.description: Recognize x-values where a line and a parabola share the same y-values. Set expressions equal, form ax^2+bx+c=0, and use the discriminant to decide real roots.

topics.title: Polynomials and Rational Functions: identifying vertical asymptotes versus holes
topics.description: Recognize canceled factors as holes and remaining denominator roots as vertical asymptotes. Factor, cancel common factors, then set unreduced denominator factors equal to zero.

topics.title: Radical and absolute value functions: solve equations combining a square root and an absolute value
topics.description: Recognize domain restrictions from the radicand and sign intervals from the absolute expression. Split into sign cases, square each case, then check roots against the original constraints.

topics.title: Exponential and logarithmic functions
topics.description: Recognize when both sides share a base or when logs are needed. Isolate the exponential, match bases if possible, otherwise take logarithms to solve.

topics.title: Intercepts, zeros, extrema, and intervals of increase/decrease
topics.description: Recognize where f increases, decreases, and where zeros and critical points lie. Solve f'(x)=0, sort critical x-values, then test f'(x) sign to mark extrema.

topics.title: Symmetry, End Behavior, and Asymptotes
topics.description: Recognize parity and asymptote types from variable behavior and graph evidence. Compare f(−x) to f(x), compare degrees and leading coefficients, and solve denominator=0 for vertical asymptotes.

topics.title: Translations, stretches, and reflections of functions
topics.description: Visualize how h, a, and k shift and scale a graph's x and y values. Replace x with (x − h), multiply by a, then add k.

topics.title: Derive a function rule from a graph or data
topics.description: Recognize constant second differences in three (x,y) points as quadratic evidence. Substitute pairs into y=ax^2+bx+c, solve for a,b,c, and verify.

topics.title: Evaluating composite functions
topics.description: Recognize the inner function applied first and the outer function applied to its output. Substitute the numeric result into the outer rule, then simplify and re-check signs and order.

topics.title: Find the inverse function
topics.description: Recognize how x and y swap and how denominators create constraints. Swap variables, clear fractions, collect y-terms, factor, and divide to isolate y.

topics.title: Domain, range, and graph relationships of inverse functions
topics.description: Recognize which x-values or outputs f excludes. Swap domain and range and confirm by solving for x or checking reflection across y=x.

topics.title: Angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal
topics.description: Recognize whether the diagram shows corresponding, alternate interior, or same‑side interior angles. Translate that relation into one equation with the variable and solve.

topics.title: Triangle congruence criteria
topics.description: You will recognize matching equal sides and the included angle between them in two triangles. Label corresponding sides and confirm the angle is included; if so, conclude congruence by SAS.

topics.title: Similar figures and proportional sides
topics.description: Recognize matching vertices and corresponding side pairs. Find k = (image B) ÷ (image A) and multiply the known side by k.

topics.title: Effect of proportional scaling on lengths, areas, and volumes
topics.description: Recognize how linear scale factor k changes lengths, areas, and volumes in geometric shapes. Compute new volume by cubing k and multiplying the original volume V_original.

topics.title: Triangle interior–exterior angle relationship
topics.description: Identify the two interior angles remote to a given exterior angle. Set the exterior measure equal to their sum and solve for the unknown variable.

topics.title: Pythagorean Theorem and Distance
topics.description: You will visualize Δx and Δy between two coordinates as legs of a right triangle. Subtract coordinates, square and sum Δx and Δy, then take the positive square root.

topics.title: Special right triangles (30°-60°-90° and 45°-45°-90° side ratios)
topics.description: Recognize angle measures and side labels (short, long, hypotenuse) from given side lengths or variables. Use the 30°-60°-90 or 45°-45°-90 ratio to solve and simplify radicals.

topics.title: Sine, Cosine, and Tangent
topics.description: Recognize the opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse relative to a given angle. Use sin=opp/hyp, cos=adj/hyp, tan=opp/adj to write and simplify the target ratio.

topics.title: Solving right triangles for angle of elevation/depression
topics.description: Recognize the horizontal distance as the adjacent leg and the unknown height as the opposite variable. Use tan(theta)=opposite/adjacent to solve for the height and simplify or approximate.

topics.title: Radii, Diameters, Circumference, and Area
topics.description: Recognize how area values link to radius and circumference using A=πr². Solve r = sqrt(A/π), then compute C=2πr and simplify in π.

topics.title: Arc length and sector area
topics.description: Recognize how a central angle determines the circle fraction for an arc or sector. Convert degrees to that fraction, then use s = fraction·2πr or A = fraction·πr².

topics.title: Central angle vs. inscribed angle
topics.description: Recognize which arc both angles intercept and compare their measures. If an angle is inscribed, take half the central measure; if central, double the inscribed measure.

topics.title: Relationships among chords, secants, and tangents
topics.description: Identify external and whole secant lengths in the diagram as concrete variables. Multiply external×whole for each secant and set tangent^2 equal to that product.

topics.title: Standard equation of a circle
topics.description: Recognize center and radius from x and y variable groups and constants. Group x and y terms, complete squares, then isolate constants to read (h,k) and r.

topics.title: Distance, Midpoints, and Partition Points (internal division of a segment)
topics.description: Recognize how a point divides a segment in a given ratio by comparing coordinates. Label r and s, then compute xP = (s·xA + r·xB)/(r+s) and yP analogously.

topics.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
topics.description: Recognize and compare slopes from two-point coordinates or y=mx+b. Equal slopes mean parallel; negative reciprocals mean perpendicular; vertical lines are undefined versus horizontal slope 0.

topics.title: Translations, Rotations, Reflections, and Dilations
topics.description: You will visualize how a point's coordinates change after each transformation. Apply specific coordinate rules in sequence and update variables after each step to compute exact final coordinates.

topics.title: Coordinate locus: translate a verbal condition into an equation for the locus
topics.description: You will recognize how each phrase maps to algebraic relations between x and y. Translate phrases, isolate terms to match standard curve forms and identify the locus family.

topics.title: Perimeter and area of polygons — equilateral triangle from perimeter
topics.description: Recognize how perimeter gives the side length and fixes area for an equilateral triangle. Divide perimeter by 3 for s, use A = (√3/4)s^2, simplify exactly then approximate.

topics.title: Area of a composite figure
topics.description: You will visualize and label each simple component and its dimensions. Break into known shapes, apply exact area formulas, then add or subtract areas while keeping units.

topics.title: Surface area and volume of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres
topics.description: Recognize the solid and its key measures: base shape, radius, height, or slant height. Choose the proper area or volume formula, write it with variables and units, substitute and compute.

topics.title: Basic equations and key features of parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas
topics.description: Recognize conic type and features from standard-form equations. Use squared-term signs and denominators as a^2,b^2, take roots to label a and get axes or asymptotes.

topics.title: Calculate mean, median, mode, and weighted average (central tendency for a small data set)
topics.description: Recognize mean, median, and mode from small data using values and frequencies. Sum ÷ count for mean; order or cumulative frequency for median; highest frequency for mode.

topics.title: Interpreting range, interquartile range (IQR), and standard deviation
topics.description: Recognize how range, IQR, and SD describe spread and react to outliers in data. Use max−min for range, Q3−Q1 for IQR, SD for typical distance.

topics.title: Boxplots, Histograms, and Frequency Tables — find a five-number summary from a frequency table
topics.description: Visualize min, Q1, median, Q3, and max via cumulative counts. Compute n, find quartile positions by cumulative rank, and read endpoints.

topics.title: How an outlier affects measures of center and spread
topics.description: Recognize how a suspect value shifts center and spread. Mark the outlier and compare mean vs median and range vs IQR using min, max, Q1, Q3.

topics.title: Population, Sample, and Simple Random Sampling
topics.description: Recognize how inclusion probability depends on population size N and sample size n. Use symmetry: inclusion probability equals n ÷ N or compute the complement with combinations.

topics.title: Identify sampling bias and nonresponse bias
topics.description: You will recognize excluded groups and skewed respondent data in survey results. Check the sampling frame and response rates to decide if undercoverage or biased nonresponse explains differences.

topics.title: Distinguish observational studies from experiments (did researchers assign treatments?)
topics.description: Recognize whether the study’s key variable is assigned or only measured using phrases like random assignment, control, or placebo. Label experimental if researchers assign treatments; otherwise label observational.

topics.title: Random assignment, control/placebo groups, blinding, and replication
topics.description: Recognize which design element targets a named bias, such as participants' expectation or confounding. Map elements to biases: prefer blinding, controls, randomization, or replication accordingly.

topics.title: Determine the appropriate population for which a study's conclusion is valid (generalizability)
topics.description: You will recognize the sample's exact characteristics and location. Compare sampled variables to each choice and reject options that broaden beyond any sampled feature.

topics.title: Determine a scatterplot's direction, form, and strength
topics.description: You will recognize a scatterplot's slope, clustering pattern, and point tightness. Scan left-to-right for rise or fall, compare linear versus curved clustering, and judge strength by tightness.

topics.title: Interpret the slope and intercept of a fitted line
topics.description: Recognize how slope and intercept connect response (y) and explanatory (x) with units. Translate slope as y change per one-unit x and judge intercept realism.

topics.title: Use a regression line to predict values and interpret residuals
topics.description: Visualize actual y versus predicted y using the regression line. Compute residual = actual y − predicted y; interpret sign and magnitude as direction and error size.

topics.title: Distinguish correlation from causation
topics.description: You will recognize when data show association between two variables but not direct cause. Check for randomization and plausible confounders; if neither is ruled out, avoid causal claims.

topics.title: Sample space and basic probability
topics.description: Visualize and list all equally likely outcomes, noting whether order or replacement matters. Then count favorable outcomes and divide by the total to compute probability.

topics.title: Probability of unions, intersections, and complements
topics.description: Recognize the complement and overlap relationships between events A and B. Use complements and subtraction to compute P(A ∪ B^c) via 1 − P(A^c ∩ B).

topics.title: Conditional Probability and Independence
topics.description: Recognize P(A ∩ B) and P(B) in the problem data. Divide P(A ∩ B) by P(B) to compute P(A|B) and simplify.

topics.title: Permutations, Combinations, and the Multiplication Counting Principle
topics.description: Recognize when order matters by checking for distinct positions or arrangements. List sequential choices, multiply options (reducing counts if no replacement), and divide by factorial only to remove order.

topics.title: Expected value of a discrete random variable
topics.description: Recognize each distinct outcome with its payoff and probability. Multiply payoffs by probabilities and add the weighted contributions to get the expected net gain.

topics.title: Combined operations with fractions, decimals, and percents
topics.description: Visualize successive decimal multipliers applied to a base price and compare the order effects. Convert percents to decimal multipliers and apply them in order, rounding only at the end.

topics.title: Ratios, proportions, unit rates, and unit conversions
topics.description: Recognize paired quantities and visualize a per one unit rate. Divide first by second for the unit rate, multiply by the new quantity, and convert only after scaling.

topics.title: Applying mean and weighted mean
topics.description: Recognize each group's total contribution to the overall mean. Multiply group means by counts, add contributions, then divide by total items.

topics.title: Contextual applications of perimeter, area, surface area, and volume
topics.description: Recognize which quantity is requested and the matching formula with units. Label the quantity, substitute converted dimensions into the formula, compute units, and check magnitude.

topics.title: Combining table, figure, and text information
topics.description: Recognize how labeled regions, textual exclusions, and table rates map to numeric areas and per-unit values. Translate shapes to areas, align units to rates, then multiply and sum region totals.

topics.title: Solving multistep cross-domain problems with an inner-border area (border-subtraction area problems)
topics.description: Visualize outer and inner rectangles and the border's effect on dimensions. Write outer dimensions in one variable, subtract twice the border to form inner area, and solve.

topics.title: Estimation and order-of-magnitude checks for answer reasonableness
topics.description: Recognize how coefficients and powers of ten represent the problem's numbers. Divide rounded coefficients, subtract exponents, then adjust the coefficient into the 1–10 range.

topics.title: Define a variable and write an equation relating quantities
topics.description: Recognize quantities and verbal relationships using a single variable and algebraic expressions. Pick one variable, write one equation tying expressions to the total, then solve and substitute to confirm.

topics.title: Build an equation, function, graph, or geometric model from a context
topics.description: Identify variables, numeric givens, and representations from the context. Write expressions for each relationship and combine them into one equation matching the stated total.

topics.title: Interpret the real-world meaning of parameters: slope, intercept, and solutions in linear models
topics.description: Recognize how slope, intercept, and a solution map to real quantities and units. Label symbols, compute numeric values with units, then translate into brief sentences.

topics.title: Check a model’s assumptions, units, domain, and applicability
topics.description: Recognize mismatched units, inputs outside the model’s data range, and violated assumptions. Convert units, check the observed domain, and reject models that assume linearity or constant rates.

topics.title: Compare different representations or models
topics.description: Recognize which model yields the larger numeric output for a specified input variable. Substitute the input into each model, compute outputs with consistent units, and compare values to decide.

topics.title: Modify an existing mathematical model when conditions change
topics.description: Recognize which variables, coefficients, or constants the new condition changes. Update only affected terms by adding or subtracting fixed amounts or multiplying coefficients by percent factors.

topics.title: Determine the passage's central idea or theme
topics.description: Recognize the passage's broad subject and main supporting points. Match one phrase for subject plus two brief points, and select the answer that matches passage evidence only.

topics.title: Determine the main idea of a single paragraph
topics.description: Recognize the sentence stating a paragraph’s purpose and scope. Underline the topic sentence and repeated subjects to choose the answer matching that scope.

topics.title: Choose an accurate summary without over-inferring
topics.description: You will recognize summaries that restate the passage's explicit main point and supporting wording. Underline explicit evidence and cross out choices adding unstated causes or consequences.

topics.title: Locate explicitly stated facts and details
topics.description: You will recognize exact words or phrases that state facts in a passage. Underline names, dates, and phrases and match wording to answer choices.

topics.title: Make a reasonable inference from the text
topics.description: You will recognize concrete textual details that imply unstated conclusions. Underline connected sentences, paraphrase suggested ideas, and check for passage statements that would be true if your paraphrase were true.

topics.title: Choose the text evidence that best supports an inference
topics.description: Recognize which specific lines contain words that imply the narrator's feeling of isolation. Read the lines before and after and eliminate choices whose wording supports a more concrete claim.

topics.title: Determine relationships among characters, events, or viewpoints
topics.description: Recognize whether one viewpoint supports, contrasts with, or responds to another from exact wording. Underline the sentences for each element, label the relationship, and confirm with a brief quote.

topics.title: Identify temporal sequence, comparison/contrast, and cause-effect relationships
topics.description: Recognize if a sentence shows sequence, contrast, or cause. Scan for concrete signal words or punctuation and label Temporal, Contrast, or Cause-Effect.

topics.title: Determine a word or phrase’s meaning from context
topics.description: You will recognize context clues, like definition, contrast, cause, or descriptive detail, surrounding the target word. Label the clue type, substitute a concise meaning, and reread to confirm sense.

topics.title: Interpret a metaphor, image, or rhetorical expression
topics.description: You will recognize the vehicle's concrete attributes and compare them to passage evidence. Identify tenor and vehicle, list vehicle attributes, and map matched attributes back to the tenor.

topics.title: Analyze how word choice affects tone and meaning
topics.description: Recognize how a marked word's connotation alters speaker attitude and tone in context. Swap it with stronger or weaker synonyms and pick the choice whose connotation matches passage attitude.

topics.title: Identify a passage or paragraph's organizational structure
topics.description: Recognize signal words and sentence relationships that reveal structure. Scan for time, cause, comparison, and problem/solution markers, then group sentences to match named patterns.

topics.title: Determine a sentence or paragraph's function in the passage
topics.description: Recognize how the marked sentence links to surrounding ideas using grammatical cues. Scan nearby sentences and signal words to label its role: background, contrast, example, summary, or forward-looking.

topics.title: Determine the author's purpose
topics.description: Recognize the passage's topic and the author's attitude toward it. Label the topic, mark intent words, and map to inform, persuade, describe, or entertain.

topics.title: Determine the narrator's perspective or the author's stance
topics.description: Recognize signal words and judgment phrases that reveal an author's stance. Label stance Endorsing, Neutral, Opposing, or Mixed and confirm with at least one supporting word or sentence.

topics.title: Determine an author's tone or attitude and its shift
topics.description: Recognize words and phrases that reveal the author’s feelings and compare them before and after a shift. Mark signal words and sentence-structure changes, then label each attitude briefly.

topics.title: Distinguish different characters' or authors' viewpoints
topics.description: Recognize each speaker's central claim and strongest supporting sentence. Label claims in one phrase, underline the key evidence, and state how viewpoints differ.

topics.title: Identify the main claim and subordinate (supporting) claims
topics.description: Recognize which sentence states the author’s central claim and which sentences provide supporting evidence. Scan topic sentences, signal words, and scope to label reasons and confirm the main claim.

topics.title: Determine whether a piece of evidence supports a claim
topics.description: Recognize whether evidence sentences directly describe the claim’s causal or comparative link. Restate the claim briefly and check if the evidence shows that link while noting alternative causes.

topics.title: Evaluate whether a claim is adequately supported by the given evidence and reasoning
topics.description: Recognize whether passage evidence directly supports an author's claim or only relates indirectly. Underline the claim, list explicit evidence, and check for causal gaps, missing data, or unstated assumptions.

topics.title: Distinguish facts, opinions, and inferences
topics.description: Recognize wording that is verifiable, judgmental, or drawn from clues in the passage. Label verifiable details as facts, judgment words (best, should) as opinions, and drawn conclusions as inferences.

topics.title: Compare paired texts' viewpoints, evidence, or methods
topics.description: You will compare each author's claim and the kind of evidence they use. Label claims, mark support as example, statistic, expert, or method, and note matches or differences.

topics.title: Synthesize information from multiple texts
topics.description: Recognize each passage's main claim and overlapping evidence. Label claims, underline overlaps, then write one sentence combining both claims and shared evidence.

topics.title: Match a chart or quantitative detail to its related statement in the passage
topics.description: Recognize passage sentences that point to a figure and its data. Underline key terms, read the exact values, and choose the claim matching those numbers.

topics.title: Explain whether a text and a figure agree or conflict
topics.description: Recognize if a passage claim and figure show the same trend. Underline the claim, match its directional prediction to figure data, then decide.

topics.title: Read a specified numeric value from a table
topics.description: Find the row and column that name the requested variable and units. Scan the leftmost column, move to the header, then read the cell value with units.

topics.title: Read a specific numeric value from a line, bar, or scatter plot
topics.description: Recognize where the target x sits between ticks or plotted points and which two values bracket it. Interpolate proportionally between bracketing heights and confirm using the vertical-axis scale and units.

topics.title: Identify increasing, decreasing, peaks, and plateaus in data trends
topics.description: Recognize rising, falling, peaking, or flat segments across the independent axis. Mark axis range, list values in order, and label the longest contiguous segment.

topics.title: Compare groups, experiments, or datasets
topics.description: You will compare groups' central values and variability in data. Rank by mean or median, breaking ties toward smaller spread to prefer more reliable results.

topics.title: Identify whether two variables show a positive, negative, or no apparent relationship
topics.description: Recognize whether paired data trends upward, downward, or stays flat. Compare first and last pairs, then check middle pairs and estimate differences to confirm direction.

topics.title: Perform proportion, difference, mean, or rate-of-change calculations
topics.description: Recognize how the dependent variable and units change across data points. Use Δy/Δx: subtract initial from final then divide to get units per unit.

topics.title: Convert and compare units, dimensions, and orders of magnitude
topics.description: You will compare numeric concentration values by recognizing units and metric prefixes. Pick mg/L as the target, convert each value stepwise (prefix→base→target), then compare magnitudes directly.

topics.title: Interpolate a value within a dataset
topics.description: Recognize the two surrounding datapoints and their coordinates on a table or graph. Use linear bracket interpolation by computing the fractional distance and applying it to y values.

topics.title: Make a limited extrapolation or prediction from a numerical trend
topics.description: Recognize short-term numerical trends by comparing stepwise growth factors between consecutive data points. Average those factors and multiply the last observed value to predict the next.

topics.title: Translate data between tables, graphs, and text
topics.description: Recognize whether text claims match numeric changes in table (two clear x,y pairs). Compute y- and x-factors for those pairs and compare them to test proportionality or trend.

topics.title: Identify a research question or a testable hypothesis
topics.description: You will recognize a manipulated variable and a specific measurable outcome in experimental descriptions. Name the IV and its levels, include units or timepoint, and write a comparative testable statement.

topics.title: Identify independent and dependent variables
topics.description: Recognize the factor deliberately changed and the outcome recorded. Label the changed factor independent and the measured outcome dependent.

topics.title: Identify controlled variables and experimental constants
topics.description: Recognize which factors stay constant versus vary in an experiment. List IV and DV, scan for factors that affect the DV, and label held items as controlled.

topics.title: Identify the control group and its purpose
topics.description: Recognize the group receiving standard conditions and compare its variables to treated groups. Confirm identical light, water, and temperature; state the control as the baseline for comparison.

topics.title: Understand the roles of replication, sample size, and randomization
topics.description: Recognize how replication, sample size, and randomization affect data strength and bias. Check randomization, compare sample sizes and variability, and weigh replicated results for confidence.

topics.title: Understand experimental steps, tools, and measurement methods
topics.description: You will recognize which recorded quantities and units correspond to experimental variables. Use units, sampling intervals, and instruments to decide dependent versus independent measurements.

topics.title: Identify a design flaw or confounding variable
topics.description: You will recognize differences in variables, equipment, timing, or sample selection across groups. Name the independent variable, list other differing conditions, and mark any plausible cause as a confound.

topics.title: Selecting a modification that improves experimental reliability or validity
topics.description: Recognize non-manipulated variables that differ between groups as potential confounds. Make those variables identical across groups and record remaining differences as controls.

topics.title: Predict the experimental result after changing one variable
topics.description: Recognize the baseline trial with matching variables and its measured result. Isolate the variable’s effect from paired trials and add or subtract that change to predict the new value.

topics.title: Design a follow-up experiment to test a new question
topics.description: You will identify the one independent variable, its concrete levels, and the dependent measurement to compare. Then state timing, random assignment, and ≥6 samples per level to isolate effects.

topicGroups.title: Evaluating Scientific Arguments and Models with Evidence

topics.title: Identify a researcher's claim, hypothesis, or model
topics.description: Recognize sentences that state predictions, data interpretations, or mechanisms using concrete wording like 'causes' or 'suggests'. Label each as HYPOTHESIS if predictive, CLAIM if interpretive, or MODEL if mechanistic.

topics.title: Select evidence that supports or weakens a scientific claim
topics.description: Recognize whether outcomes match the claim's predicted effect and key manipulated variables. Compare conditions and decide if the reported evidence supports, contradicts, or is irrelevant to the claim.

topics.title: Judge whether a conclusion goes beyond what the data support
topics.description: Recognize conclusions that overstate data by comparing means, sample sizes, and spreads in the table. Flag overlaps, tiny samples, or confounders as reasons to reject broad causal claims.

topics.title: Distinguish correlation from causal explanation
topics.description: You will recognize whether data show covariation or causal mechanism by comparing variable patterns and directions. Confirm correlation patterns, then search for a third variable or experimental control.

topics.title: Compare similarities and differences between two or more scientific models
topics.description: Compare predictors, assumptions, and observed variables each model links to outcomes. Create a model-feature matrix, mark linked variables, and find one prediction only one model makes.

topics.title: Identify assumptions underlying a scientific model
topics.description: You will recognize which model elements lack supporting data or controlled variables. List treated-as-constant factors, match them to experimental conditions, and flag any without evidence.

topics.title: Decide which viewpoint a new piece of evidence supports
topics.description: Recognize which model the new numeric result aligns with by comparing predicted outcomes and measured variables. Match predicted direction and magnitude, then check controls for key alternative explanations.

topics.title: Revise a prediction or model based on evidence
topics.description: Recognize where predictions diverge from data and which variables align with that change. Quantify the gap and minimally update the model to yield a new testable prediction.

topics.title: Infer a mechanism that explains observed experimental results
topics.description: Recognize which measured variable changed most and compare its magnitude to other data. Match that change to an immediate causal step and reject mechanisms requiring absent or slow effects.

topics.title: Accurately understand the issue and the given stance
topics.description: You will recognize the prompt's core claim and the exact stance wording to address. Restate the issue, label the stance, and list two limits to guide your thesis.

topics.title: State a clear, defensible central claim
topics.description: Recognize a concise thesis sentence that directly answers the prompt and signals purpose. Use the Claim-Backbone writing moves: state stance, add a scope qualifier, and attach one specific reason.

topics.title: Analyze your own position and its relationship to at least one provided position
topics.description: Compare one clear agreement or disagreement between your thesis and the provided position. Briefly state your thesis, give one concrete example, and explain how it refines your claim.

topics.title: Address counterarguments, limitations, or complexity
topics.description: Recognize concise opposing claims and evidence that reveal limitations. Acknowledge briefly with a precise qualifier, then refute or incorporate it to strengthen your thesis.

topics.title: Provide logical reasons for a paragraph subclaim
topics.description: Recognize concise reasons and brief facts that support a paragraph subclaim. Use Claim‑Reason‑Bridge: state one specific reason, add a short fact, then link it to the main claim.

topics.title: Use concrete examples or evidence
topics.description: You will recognize the most focused concrete example and its two vivid, relevant details. Pick one example, describe two specific details, and name exactly how it supports the claim.

topics.title: Explain how evidence supports a claim
topics.description: You will recognize how specific evidence links to a claim and thesis. Restate the claim and evidence, explain the causal mechanism, and connect back to the thesis.

topics.title: Elaborate effects, consequences, and implications
topics.description: Recognize immediate and broader consequences that support your thesis. Name one direct effect, ask “So what?”, then add a brief linking sentence as a writing move.

topics.title: Constructing a clear introduction, body, and conclusion
topics.description: Visualize how the claim, paragraph reasons, and evidence align. Write one-sentence intro purpose, one linking sentence per body, and a concluding restatement tying the claim to context.

topics.title: Ordering the progression of arguments
topics.description: Recognize which reasons directly support the claim and which extend or illustrate it. Label primaries and secondaries, place primaries first, then order by strength and clarity.

topics.title: Using sentence-level and paragraph-level cohesion
topics.description: Recognize weak or missing topic sentences and unclear links between paragraphs. Strengthen topic sentences, use linking phrases, or add brief transitional sentences.

topics.title: Maintain overall focus and paragraph unity
topics.description: Recognize sentences that stray from the thesis or fail paragraph unity. Anchor, prune, then add a closing line linking content to the claim using precise writing moves.

topics.title: Use accurate, clear, and context-appropriate word choice
topics.description: Recognize the target word and its grammatical function and tone. Choose one precise alternative that preserves purpose or one that changes tone, then read aloud to check clarity.

topics.title: Use varied and controlled sentence structures
topics.description: Recognize three consecutive sentences that share length or grammatical structure. Convert one sentence by combining, splitting, or beginning with a subordinate clause and adjust punctuation for natural flow.

topics.title: Maintain consistent tone and register
topics.description: You will recognize words and constructions that clash with a formal register. Choose a tone anchor and edit flagged segments to align grammar, diction, and evidence with that register.

topics.title: Control grammar, usage, spelling, and punctuation errors
topics.description: Recognize missing or extra words and errors in agreement, spelling, and punctuation within a sentence. Fix one issue, then reorder words and reread for tone.
